title: Pipeline run.py shows full stage stderr on failure
problem: pipeline/run.py truncates failed-stage output to the first 5 lines via 'output.strip().splitlines()[:5]' at line 333. When a stage retries internally (auto_refine retries up to 3 times, executor retries each step), the truncation hides attempts 2 and 3, the final error, and any usage blocks emitted between attempts. Operators see only the early lines and have no way to diagnose what actually went wrong. This was flagged in the previous session's handoff as an open thread and is now blocking real debugging.
description: Remove the [:5] truncation from pipeline/run.py's failure output handling and emit the full stage output instead. Stage output is already captured in memory (stdout_text/stderr_text from run_stage); printing it in full on failure is essentially free and the right default. Optionally guard against pathological cases (>2000 lines) with a much higher cap, but the default should be 'show everything on failure'.
scope: 1) Edit pipeline/run.py around line 332-334: replace 'for line in output.strip().splitlines()[:5]:' with a loop that prints all lines (or with a much higher cap like 500 lines plus a 'truncated' notice if exceeded). 2) Verify that the success-path output (which uses last_line at line 324) is unaffected. 3) Manually trigger a stage failure (e.g. break the executor temporarily) and confirm the full retry trace and final error appear in run.py output. 4) Update docs/reference/cli-tools.md entry for run.py if it documents the truncation behavior. Out of scope: changing what stages write to stderr, adding a separate per-stage log file, changing the success-path summary, the executor stdout/stderr fix (separate ticket).
context: Flagged as open thread in session 7d668bb1 handoff (note #158). Hit hard this session during pipeline runs e3976ee9 and c7958c29: refiner failed on attempts 2 and 3 with errors we never saw, and the executor's silent commit failures were impossible to diagnose without reading source. Sister ticket: executor surfaces git stdout on commit failures.
